summary: Defines the sip-trunking-capability link relation type that an enterprise telephony network can use to get a document describing a provider's SIP trunking capabilities and requirements, helping enable peering.

plainLanguage.summary: This link relation identifies a web resource that describes an ITSP's SIP trunking capabilities and configuration needs. An enterprise network can discover the document and use its machine-readable parameters.

questions: how to discover sip trunk requirements
what is the sip-trunking-capability link relation
what is a capability set document
subtitle: Defines a link relation for discovering an ITSP's SIP trunk capability document.

tldr.problem: An enterprise SIP network may need an ITSP's capabilities and configuration requirements to establish SIP trunking.
tldr.mechanism: The sip-trunking-capability link relation points to a structured capability set document hosted by the ITSP; the example discovers it through WebFinger.
tldr.outcome: The relation is registered in the Link Relation Types registry, with caution advised for sensitive information sent over insecure channels.

today: RFC 9409 is an Informational RFC. The unit metadata does not list it as obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: The SIP Trunking Capability Relation
sections.content:
RFC 8288 defines a way to indicate relationships between Web resources. RFC 9409 defines the sip-trunking-capability relation so potential SIP peers can exchange capability information.

An ITSP can use the relation on a Web resource to provide a structured capability set document. The RFC says enterprise telephony devices can retrieve that document to automate establishment of SIP trunking.
sections.plainLanguage: The relation labels a link to an ITSP capability document. The document describes technical requirements for peering.

sections.title: The Capability Set Document
sections.content:
The ITSP hosts the capability set document. Its location may be preconfigured and provided to each peer, or a central resource may generate it dynamically based on URIs supplied by the peering device.

The document contains structured, machine-readable parameters that can be converted into configuration data to meet the ITSP's communication requirements. The format is described in the referenced Automatic Peering for SIP Trunks work-in-progress document.
sections.plainLanguage: The document lists configuration parameters in a machine-readable form. A device can convert those parameters into settings.

sections.title: Discovering the Document with WebFinger
sections.content:
In the example, an enterprise network device requests the sip-trunking-capability relation from the ITSP's well-known WebFinger URI. The response contains an href attribute that gives the capability set document's location.

The RFC says the ITSP may use an authentication framework such as OAuth 2.0 to determine the enterprise network's identity and provide the appropriate document.
sections.plainLanguage: The example uses WebFinger to ask the ITSP where its capability document is. The response supplies a link to that document.
